title: GRST1: coherent retained-block search with linear source count

claims.statement: For GRST1 in proof.md, for every integer N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N), k=n+20 and use the exact coherent retained-block search configuration specified there, including its finite n=1 branch. Unconditional entire-secret recovery has probability greater than 2/3. On every execution branch this same algorithm has total sequential work T=O(2^(n/2) n^2 (log2 n)^2) for n>=2, with fixed absolute cost for n=1, jointly with all other resource bounds and the clean-input tolerance below. All constants are absolute. The supported envelope B(n)=2^(n/2) n^2 (log2 n)^2 for n>=2 has exact growth index 1. Complete uniform circuits, controller, addressing, preprocessing and acquisition accounting are proved in proof.md.

On every execution branch this same algorithm has peak classical storage S_C=O(n) bits, jointly with all other resource bounds and the clean-input tolerance below. All constants are absolute. The supported envelope B(n)=n has exact growth index 0. Complete uniform circuits, controller, addressing, preprocessing and acquisition accounting are proved in proof.md.

Unconditional entire-secret recovery has probability greater than 2/3. On every execution branch this same algorithm has total acquired source count Q=n+20=O(n), jointly with all other resource bounds and the clean-input tolerance below. All constants are absolute. For the same GRST1 algorithm/configuration in proof.md, for every N>=2 and every s, n=ceil(log2 N) and actual acquired count Q=n+20, the guaranteed malformed-copy threshold is tau(n,Q)=0. All Q copies must be independent ideal coset states. Under this promise unconditional full-secret success is greater than 2/3 and all four resource bounds hold jointly on every branch. No behavior for malformed copies or impossibility of positive tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed-sample count among Q acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
